pageCache.pageTitle: Admission Arrangements | Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School
Welcome to our Website
Admission Arrangements
Admissions
As a voluntary controlled school, our admissions are managed by Bracknell Forest Council. We have no influence over their decisions and allocation of places. In the first instance, you should always contact the admissions team with any queries rather than the school directly.Since many prospective parents visit this site it may be useful for you to know that in recent years the number of children joining the school from the immediate catchment area has varied and that a number of children each year have been admitted from outside of catchment, for reference this number has been as high as 8.The school has a planned admission number each year of 30 children.Winkfield St Mary’s serves the area of Winkfield, Winkfield Row and Maidens Green.Applications for places at this school will be considered in the following order of priority:
Children with an Education Health and Care Plan that names a specific school must, by law, be admitted to that school. After this requirement has been satisfied the following rules will apply:
(A) Looked After Children and all previously looked after children. Previously looked after children are children who were looked after, but ceased to be so because they were adopted (or became subject to a child arrangements order or special guardianship order) immediately following having been looked after.
(B) Children who appear to have been in state care outside of England and ceased to be in state care as a result of being adopted
(C) Children who have either medical or social grounds for admission to a particular school. This evidence must set out the particular reason why the school in question is the only suitable school and the difficulties caused if the child had to attend another school. The LA’s decision in these matters is final.
(D) Children of staff at a particular school. Where a member of staff has been employed at the school for two or more years at the time at which the application for admission to the school is made and/or the member of staff is recruited to fill a vacant post for which there is demonstrable skill shortage.
(E) Children who live in the designated area of the school and who have a sibling who will still be attending the school at the time of the child’s admission. Children must be living in the designated area at the closing date of 15 January 2024 to be considered under this criterion.
(F) Children who live in the designated area of the school. Children must be living in the designated area at the closing date of 15 January 2024 to be considered under this criterion.
(G) Children who do not live in the designated area of the school but who have a sibling who will still be attending the school at the time of the child’s admission
(H) All other children
Parents requesting a place for their child are welcome to visit the school by prior appointment - we encourage you to let us know if you or your child require support with access in order that we can make reasonable adjustments. Applications for places at schools in Bracknell Forest are centrally managed by the LA and administered each spring for the following academic year. You can apply for a place for your child either online (using the link below) or by contacting the School Admissions Team at:School Admissions TeamTime SquareMarket StreetBracknellRG12 1JDTel: 01344 354023
School.admissions@bracknell-forest.gov.uk
For further information, visit the Bracknell Forest school admissions website
Children who are accepted for admission to the school are invited to spend an afternoon in their class during the term prior to their starting. Further visits can be arranged at the discretion of the class teacher and parents. If your child is refused admission, you have the right of appeal to an Independent Panel.
Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School

pageCache.text:
Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School
Welcome to our Website
Autism Fast Responder
Winkfield St Mary's: Supporting Autism Inclusion
As a school we aim to foster an environment in which inclusion and happiness are at the heart of everything we do.
In April 2025, we took an important step to support this objective and the learning outcomes of pupils. The school is proud to participate in the Beyond Autism Fast Responder ® initiative.
The programme supports autistic pupils, schools and carers, with needs-led inclusive solutions, in the hope of addressing the disproportionate and growing number of suspensions and permanent exclusions of pupils.
To reduce this national picture, it is crucial that autistic children access learning in environments that are inclusive and supportive of their needs. At Winkfield St Mary’s we are committed to providing inclusive learning environments. Our quality first teaching ethos ensures staff are confident in teaching SEN pupils, whilst working with pupils and wider support networks to ensure we have the right strategies, resources and processes to enable proactive approach to behaviours that challenge.
In support of this programme, we have dedicated resources and leads to manage the programme and its objectives.
It's important to note that our Beyond Autism Fast Responders ® support a range of pupil needs.
Those with or without an EHCP

Governing Body Information
Collecting and publishing Governing Board Diversity Data
The governors of Winkfield St Mary's believe it is important that boards reflect the diversity of the school communities they serve. Diverse boards promote inclusive school environments and provide diverse role models for staff and young people.
The governors will collect data on the diversity of the board, including data on age, gender and ethnicity. They will use that data to inform their recruitment and training needs and ensure there is always a diverse range of perspectives around the table to support robust decision making.
Due to our relatively small governing board, we will not publish this diversity data online as individual governors could be identified and we have a legal obligation to protect their personal data.
Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Governors | Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School
Welcome to our Website
Governors
The Governing Body of Winkfield St Mary's Church of England Primary School
The governors of Winkfield St Mary’s are a group of people who have a strong interest in the school and in education, and who are responsible for the overall management of the school. For example, they make sure that the pupils are taught the national curriculum, that the school spends its money wisely and that the school buildings are kept in good repair. They make policy decisions about staffing, health and safety, collective worship, the curriculum and many other things that affect the running of the school. Governors work very closely with the Head Teacher. Winkfield St Mary has a constitution of 13 governors of which a minimum of 2 must be represented by the Parent body and each term of office for each governor is usually held for 4 years:
The governing body invites additional people to become associate members from time to time. They do not have voting rights, but bring specific skills or experience to meetings. For details of our current governors, see our "Meet The Governors" page.
2 appointed by the church authorities
1 nominated by the local education authority
Governing Body Structure and Committee Responsibilities
Governance is delivered through the Full Governing Body which usually meets ten times a year and its supporting committees. There is one committee for Finance which meets three times a year and two special purpose committees for reviewing Pay and the Headteacher's target setting and performance management.The Finance Committee focuses on finance, budgeting and monitoring of expenditure, personnel matters and premises including health and safety.
The Clerk to the Governing Body can be contacted via the school with any queries you may have about the governing body, or if you want to know more about becoming a governor. Any queries regarding individual children should always be discussed with the class teacher or Head Teacher in the first instance

pageCache.pageTitle: Meet The Governors | Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School
Welcome to our Website
Meet The Governors
Julian Brecknock - LA Governor/Chair
I have been a governor at Winkfield St Mary’s since 2012 and have held many roles in that time including SEN link, Curriculum link and more recently Co-Chair and currently Chair. I got into school governance to help improve my understanding of how schools work and how I can use my skills in negotiation and strategic planning to help. I most enjoy visiting the school when it is open, there’s an energy and positive atmosphere that is unique to Winkfield St Mary's.
Outside of Governance I like to volunteer at a local dog rescue centre and spend time with my family, including my two teenage children, both of whom attended Winkfield St Mary’s and are now in their final years of secondary education.
John Sawford - Co-opted Governor/Vice Chair
I am now into my third year as a co-opted Governor having joined in September 2021. My two grown up sons attended St Mary’s in the late 90’s and I live locally, so when I saw the school was looking for Governors I had no hesitation in applying. Having retired back in 2020 from a career in Global Finance and General Management, I believe my professional experience brings a different skill set into the School Governance environment. Having been elected into the role of Vice Chair for this academic year, living locally and being retired allows me to be very participative in support of the school.
I look forward to continue working with Mrs Tomkins and her Senior Leadership Team as we strive to make Winkfield St Mary’s the primary school of choice in our community.
Louise Farrar - Co-opted Governor
It is a privilege to be a member of the Governing Board at Winkfield St Mary’s. I have been teaching for 30 years, primarily in Early Years and Key Stage 1 and have held a variety of leadership roles. I am currently Head of Pre Prep at Lambrook School with a particular interest in pupil wellbeing and curriculum development. I very much enjoy using my skills and knowledge to support the Head, staff and Governing Board to ensure the best possible education for each pupil and to ensure that the school continues to thrive.
Lisa Fazey - Staff Governor
Being appointed as staff Governor at Winkfield is a privilege. Having worked at St Mary's, in various roles, for the past 10 years has enabled me to gain a deeper understanding of the education system and how to support children on their learning journey. Being able to help nurture each child's learning along with building relationships with parents is an important part of my role as a class teacher. My family and friends are really important to me and I love spending time with them, whether that maybe be a game of badminton or a meal together. I hope to continue building upon our schools firm foundations by following our school and Christian values.
Steven West - Co-opted Governor
Rachel Tomkins - Head Teacher
I have had the privilege of being the Headteacher at Winkfield St Mary’s since September 2022. With over 12 years of teaching experience across the primary phase, I also hold a specialism in Early Years education and Special Educational Needs (SEN). I am dedicated to ensuring that every child, regardless of their individual challenges, receives the support and encouragement they need to reach their full potential.
Throughout my career, I have worked with a wide range of students, always striving to create an inclusive environment where every child feels valued and can succeed. I believe in nurturing both academic and emotional growth, fostering resilience, and encouraging a love of learning through a multitude of awe and wonder experiences. As Headteacher, I am committed to working closely with our families, staff, and governors to ensure that Winkfield St Mary’s continues to be a school where every child feels supported and inspired. I look forward to the journey ahead and am excited to continue making a positive impact on the lives of our children.
Holly Moore - Co-opted Governor
I originally joined Winkfield St Mary's as the Deputy Headteacher and SENCO in September 2022 and joined the governing body as an Associate Governor. In September 2025, I became a Deputy Headteacher at a Specialist Primary School in Surrey and re-joined the WSM governing body as a co-opted and safeguarding governor. My passion is ensuring every child has access to an appropriate education and that all children have the opportunity to achieve their full potential.
Cesar Fraguela Rodriguez - Parent Governor
I joined the Governing Board as a Parent Governor in December 2024. I moved from Spain to Bracknell in 2008. I work as a Finance Manager for an IT company. I am looking forward to learning more about the education system and working with the other Governors and Winkfield St Mary’s school staff to continue to deliver an optimal environment for the development of the children.
Suki Hayes - Parent Governor
I became Parent Governor in January 2024 and have learnt so much already within my first year. I currently have a daughter in Year 3 at Winkfield St Mary's and another who will hopefully join in September 2026. I have worked for a Local Authority for over 14 years within the Children and Young People's Disability Service. This is a multi-professional service with a statutory responsibility for education and social care for children and young people with SEND. As the Specialist Services Manager, I am responsible for ensuring that all our processes are carried out in-line with our statutory duties. My role includes the monitoring of budgets and having a close working relationship with multi-agencies, such as health and schools. I work closely with the SEN team and assist with supporting in advice for EHCPs in relation to social care and commissioning. I was a Borough Councillor for Bracknell Forest for 12 years from 2011 - 2023. During this time, I sat on boards and panels for children and young people and education, including the School Accountability Board and I also Chaired the Corporate Parent Advisory Panel for the last 4 years whilst elected. The area of governance that I am most interested in is SEND and feel that my knowledge and experience are of benefit. I am an active member of the PTA and I have thoroughly enjoyed embracing and becoming a part of the school community. I want to see the school thrive and for the children to have access to the best facilities and teaching opportunities and to work together and ensure that whilst providing them an enjoyable setting for learning, they are also safeguarded and provided the best support.
Rachel Moss - Clerk to Governors
Debbie Lewis - Co-opted Governor
As a newly committed school governor I am looking forward to getting involved with St Mary’s once again. My children previously attended the school and I was always an active parent, being part of the PTA. I currently run my own business and have extensive corporate experience which I hope will be useful. I have also volunteered for 4 years with the British Dyslexia Association, so hoping this is something I can utilise as the SEN link governor.
I have lived in Winkfield Row for over 23 years and truly appreciate the amazing community we have. I am honoured to support the school and help every child thrive.
Helen Evans - Deputy Headteacher/Associate Governor
I have taught at Winkfield St Mary’s in a range of roles and year groups since in 2013. It is a very special school to me! In September 2025 I had the privilege of becoming Deputy Headteacher and SENDCO. I am an Associate Governor and support the governing board with SEND and school development alongside the Headteacher. I am passionate about enabling all children to flourish and achieve their individual, full potential.
Bethany Beckford - Co-Opted Governor
I joined the WSM Governing Board in December 2024.
I have two sons, Isaac and Finley (11 and 14 years old) both who attended Winkfield St Marys. I have 20 years of experience working in both the Pharmaceutical and Food industries primarily as an Analytical Chemist. I started my career in the laboratory in Research, and have since moved through different roles including Supply Chain and finally into Scientific Project Management, leading teams to deliver large projects for internal and external clients.In April 2024 I stepped back from my working life to take a career break, giving more time to focus on my family, the local community and my house renovation. This has allowed more time to support WSM and I am really looking forward to supporting the school in its journey of continuous improvement for the pupils and staff.
Sharon Cakebread - Foundation Governor
Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Online Safety | Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Winkfield St Mary's CE Primary School
Welcome to our Website
Online Safety
Online Safety is vitally important these days and is something that we talk frequently to the children about. Partly because the world is constantly changing and partly because we have children and teenagers of our own. It's hard to keep up with changes in technology and the current risks so this is a particular area where home and school have to work in partnership .
The vast majority of our children have access to the internet outside school via all manner of devices. We heavily rely on, and expect parents to engage with internet safety, so children can take safe risks and practice skills learnt in school at home. The internet is a great place to create, connect and share. We firmly believe that a better internet starts with us. It’s a new and exciting place that we all have to engage with for the sake of our children.
We share an Online Safety Newsletter with our parents. This can be found by clicking the Safeguarding tab and scroll down to view the latest and previous newsletters.
These are the SMART rules we use we use in school for all discussions on e-safety.

Safeguarding for Children
What is safeguarding?
Safeguarding is everybody looking after your health, safety and welfare.
How do we safeguard you at Winkfield St Mary's?
What should we do if we are worried about something?
Speak to an adult at school if you are worried about something, it could be your teacher, a teaching assistant or lunchtime supervisor.
Your safeguarding leads are:
Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL)
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL)
Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL)
Useful Safeguarding Websites (Click on the blue words to go to the website)
Childline- a free, private and confidential service where you can talk about anything. Whatever your worry, whenever you need help, we're here for you online, on the phone, anytime.
Anti-Bullying Alliance- The Anti-Bullying Alliance is a coalition of organisations and individuals that are united against bullying.
Think U Know - The site has information and games to help you to learn about online safety.
Common Sense Media - Use the search box at the top to search for a game or app. There will be a Common Sense Media review which includes the information you need to help you make decisions about the suitability of a game. It also has useful parent and child reviews for each game
